title: Meeting Room Bookings
statement:
A meeting room has **n** bookings. Booking i occupies the room for every minute from l[i] to r[i], inclusive. The bookings are in random order and they may overlap.

The manager wants a clean schedule: merge all bookings that **share at least one minute** into one block, repeatedly, until no two blocks share a minute. Note that [1, 3] and [4, 6] do **not** share a minute, so they stay separate; [1, 3] and [3, 6] share minute 3 and become [1, 6].

Print the final blocks sorted by their start.
input:
The first line contains an integer **n**.

Each of the next n lines contains two integers l[i] and r[i].
output: On the first line print k, the number of blocks. Then print k lines, each with the start and end of a block, in increasing order of start.
hints: Sort the bookings by their start time.
Walk through the sorted list and keep the current block. If the next booking starts at or before the end of the current block, extend the block; otherwise start a new block.
editorial:
Sort the intervals by l. Keep a list of merged blocks. For each interval in order: if the list is empty or `l > last.end`, append a new block; otherwise set `last.end = max(last.end, r)`. After sorting, any interval that overlaps an earlier block must overlap the last block, so one pass is enough.

Complexity: O(n log n) for sorting.
